senses.gloss: to smooth, rub, polish, sharpen; to smear over, plaster.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 14:5">Kel. XIV, 5</cite> <he>משיְשׁוּפֶינּוּ</he> (Mish. ed. <he>משישׁוּפֶנּוּ</he>; Ar. <he>משיְשַׁפֶּנּוּ</he>, fr. <cite ref="U01734"><he>שָׁפָה</he> I</cite>) a sword becomes susceptible of uncleanness when it is furbished. Ib. XVI, 1 <he>משיְשׁוּפם בעור הדג</he> when he smooths them by rubbing with the skin of a fish; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 20b">Snh. 20ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Nedarim 56b:3">Ned. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>משיְשַׁפֵּם</he> (Rashi <he>משישופם</he>). Kel. l. c. <he>גמר שלא לָשׁוּף</he> if he decided not to smooth them.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1:8">Y. Ber. III, 5ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>לאיזה דבר הוא שָׁפָהּ</he> for what purpose should he polish it? <cite ref="Chullin 25a">Ḥull. 25ᵃ</cite>, sq.; <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 2:10">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. II, 10</cite>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Tahorot 6:12">Tosef. Toh. VI, 12</cite> <he>ושָׁפָה את רוקו</he> and she rubbed his spittle off (with her foot); <he>שָׁפוֹת וכ׳</he> (<he>להיות</he>) … <he>שכן</he> for it is the habit of Israelitish women during menstruation to rub off &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:32">Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵇ</cite> top <he>רוקק ושָׁף</he> he spits on the stone pavement and rubs it out (with his foot).
<cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 1:10">M. Kat. I, 10</cite> <he>שָׁפִין את הסדקין</he> you may plaster over the rifts in the roof (during the festive week).
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 20:3">Sabb. XX, 3</cite> <he>ולא שפין אותן</he> nor must you rub them (with the hand to cleanse them).
<cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 1:8">Eduy. I, 8</cite> <he>שורין ושפין וכ׳</he> you must observe levitical cleanness when you soak them and rub (your body) with them.
<cite ref="Shabbat 75b:3">Sabb. 75ᵇ</cite> <he>השף בין העמודים</he> he who rubs (smooths skins) between columns; Y. ib. VII, 10ᶜ bot. <he>השף את העור על גבי העמוד</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 30:1">Kel. XXX, 1</cite> <he>שָׁפָן בשופין</he> files them with a file.
<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 2:7">Pes. II, 7</cite> <he>אבל שָׁפָה היא וכ׳</he> but she may rub (the bran) dry over her body (to soften her skin); a. fr.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 6">Gen. R. s. 6</cite>; Midr. Sam. ch. IX.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 315:6">Sifré Deut. 315</cite> <he>שיהו חטים שָׁפוֹת זו וכ׳</he> that wheat grains rub against one another and drop &c., v. <cite ref="O01044"><he>סֹלֶת</he></cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 944">Yalk. ib. 944</cite>.—

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 4:13">Midr. Till. to Ps. IV, 7</cite> <he>וישראל … ואתם באים לָשׁוּף אותה מן העקב</he> and the Israelites say to them (the gentiles asking for a share in the hereafter), in how many troubles … we surrendered our lives for the sanctification of the Lord, and you want to stamp it (all this good) out of your heels (out of the ground)?; (ed. Bub. <he>אותם על העקב</he>, corr. acc.); Yalk. ib. 627 <he>לשוף עצמיכם מן העקב</he> (corr. acc.).—[<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 92:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII</cite> <he>וישופני עקב</he>, v. <cite ref="U00490"><he>שׁוּף</he> I</cite>.]

senses.gloss: to be rubbed off, made smooth, level.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 10:4">Tosef. B. Kam. X, 4</cite> <he>מטבע ונ׳</he> if he took by force a coin, and it became rubbed off (effaced).

<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Metzia 11:8">Tosef. B. Mets. XI, 8</cite> <he>מוציא אדם זבלו … כדי שיִישּׁוֹף וכ׳</he> a man may take out his material for dung and place it in front of his house, that it may be stamped upon by the feet of man and beast; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 30a">B. Kam. 30ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 81b">81ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 118b:4">B. Mets. 118ᵇ</cite> <he>כדי שיהא נישוף</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 28b:13">B. Kam. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>נשוף באבן</he> (Ms. F. <he>ונושף</he>, read: <cite ref="U01792"><he>נִישָּׁף</he></cite>) was smashed against a stone; (Y. ib. III, 3ᶜ top <cite ref="H00040"><he>נחבט</he></cite>).—V. <cite ref="U01792"><he>שָׁפַף</he></cite>.
